events.title: Ron's family dish
events.premise: {self} cooks something nobody has seen him make before: a dish with a name written on an old order slip. {b} asks where it's from.

events.title: a call from Ron's sister
events.premise: On speaker by accident: Ron's sister Yael asks if he's told the house about the shop yet. {b} heard every word.

events.title: the restaurant question
events.premise: {self} shows {b} a bank book and a photo of a shuttered shop front. 'I could reopen it. Next spring. If I leave soon.'

effects.leaveReason: left to reopen his family's restaurant

events.title: Kai films the moment
events.premise: {b} is telling a real story about their family when they notice {self}'s phone is pointed at them, recording.

events.title: the numbers don't add up
events.premise: In the arcade, a brand manager asks {self} for his analytics in front of {b}. 'The engagement rate is... unusual.'

events.title: Kai, unedited
events.premise: {self} deletes the editing app in front of {b}. 'One video. No cuts. Just me, saying the numbers were fake.'

events.title: Shai's fear
events.premise: {self} is watering the backyard plants and, for once, answers a question about himself. 'I'm thirty-one. Everyone I know is married.'

events.title: a family introduction
events.premise: {self}'s mother calls about someone she met through friends in Jerusalem. {b} hears her asking why he still has not called.

events.title: Shai decides
events.premise: {self} tells {b} he promised his mother a visit and a coffee with her friend's daughter. 'I want to make my own decision. I just do not want to hurt her.'

effects.leaveReason: went home to try the marriage meeting

events.title: late-night texts
events.premise: 1 a.m. {self}'s phone buzzes face-down on the sofa, again and again. She flips it over too fast. {b} notices.

fact.subject: self
fact.content: {self} gets late-night messages from someone she won't name.

events.title: the ex appears
events.premise: At the cafe with {b}, {self} freezes. Her ex, Daniel, is at the counter, waving. 'Maya! I texted you I'd be here.'

events.title: Maya's choice
events.premise: {self} shows {b} her phone: a message to Daniel, unsent. 'If I send this, it's over. Will you stay while I do it?'

events.title: Shira's block
events.premise: {self} has played the same four chords for an hour on the backyard. When {b} comes up, she asks: 'Tell me something true. I'm out.'

events.title: the honest conversation
events.premise: Over cold tea, {b} turns Shira's favorite question back on her. 'Say the real thing. Why are you here?'

events.title: the new song
events.premise: A packed basement. {self} plays a song nobody has heard, written after one honest conversation. {b} is in the front row.

effects.leaveReason: left for a recording contract in London

events.title: a slip
events.premise: {self} almost says something about their past, then changes the subject a little too fast. {b} notices.

fact.subject: self
fact.content: {self} is hiding something about their past.

events.title: it comes out
events.premise: {b} asks {self} directly. There's no changing the subject this time.

events.title: after the secret
events.premise: {self} finds {b} on the backyard. 'Thanks for not making it weird. Well. Weirder.'

events.title: second thoughts
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} they're not sure this city, or this life, is the right one.

events.title: pressure from outside
events.premise: A phone call with an offer {self} can't easily refuse. {b} sees their face change.

events.title: the decision
events.premise: {self} tells {b} they've made a decision about whether to stay.

effects.leaveReason: took the offer and moved on

events.title: the buzzing phone
events.premise: {self}'s phone keeps buzzing with one name. They turn it face down. {b} saw the name.

fact.subject: self
fact.content: {self} keeps getting messages from an ex.

events.title: the past walks in
events.premise: {self}'s ex walks into the cafe where {self} and {b} are sitting.

events.title: closing the door
events.premise: {self} deletes a contact with {b} watching. 'Okay. Done. Don't let me undo it.'

events.title: stuck
events.premise: {self} has been staring at the same blank page all evening. {b} brings tea.

events.title: something true
events.premise: {b} asks {self} the question nobody asks. {self} answers it.

events.title: the breakthrough
events.premise: {self} shows {b} the finished thing. It's good. It's really good.

events.title: a call from home
events.premise: {self}'s family calls. Afterwards, {b} finds them sitting very still on the backyard.

events.title: family visits
events.premise: {self}'s younger sibling shows up unannounced and immediately tells {b} embarrassing stories.

events.title: stay or go home
events.premise: {self} asks {b} whether they'd miss them if they went home for good.

events.title: good news from the kitchen
events.premise: {self} comes home buzzing and tells {b} the head chef put one of {self}'s dishes on the menu this week.

events.title: kitchen gossip
events.premise: {b} drops by {place} on {self}'s break. {self} whispers the latest: the sous-chef and a waiter keep sneaking out back together, and the whole kitchen knows.

events.title: a quiet dream
events.premise: {self} admits something to {b}: they've been saving in secret to open a tiny place of their own one day. Nobody else knows yet.

events.title: a rough shift
events.premise: {self} drops onto the sofa next to {b}: the dishwasher broke mid-service and they scrubbed pans by hand all night. It's funny now, mostly.

events.title: someone quit
events.premise: {b} visits {place} and {self} pulls them aside: the line cook everyone liked quit yesterday by text, and nobody knows why.

events.title: a confession
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} that they don't really love cooking anymore, not like they used to. They've never said it out loud.

events.title: after the night shift
events.premise: {self} gets home at dawn and tells {b} about the night: a baby was born in the hospital elevator, and {self} helped deliver it.

events.title: hospital gossip
events.premise: {b} brings coffee to {place}. {self} shares the ward's big story: two doctors who supposedly can't stand each other were seen holding hands in the parking lot.

events.title: a job elsewhere
events.premise: {self} quietly tells {b} they applied for a job at a hospital in another city. Nothing is decided, and nobody else knows.

events.title: a new trainee
events.premise: {self} tells {b} they've been put in charge of a new trainee, who has already nicknamed them 'the scary one'.

events.title: the trainee's love life
events.premise: {b} stops by {place}. Between patients, {self} spills it: the trainee is dating a nurse's ex from the next ward, and it's getting messy.

events.title: an old mistake
events.premise: {self} tells {b} about a mistake from their first year that still keeps them up some nights. They've never told the house.

events.title: a post takes off
events.premise: {self} shows {b} their phone: one of their posts got thousands of views overnight, and strangers are leaving comments.

events.title: scene gossip
events.premise: {b} catches up with {self} at {place}. {self} leans in: a well-known local artist got caught copying someone's work, and everyone is pretending not to talk about it.

events.title: the secret account
events.premise: {self} confesses to {b} that they run an anonymous account nobody in the house knows about. That's where their real work goes.

events.title: a callback
events.premise: {self} tells {b} they got a callback for something big and can't stop pacing the room.

events.title: backstage rumors
events.premise: {b} visits {place} before rehearsal. {self} has gossip: the lead and the director had a shouting match yesterday, and someone might get replaced.

events.title: stage fright
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} that they almost skipped the audition, and that they freeze on stage more often than anyone knows.

events.title: a big order
events.premise: {self} tells {b} a client just ordered a full set of custom furniture, the biggest job they've ever had.

events.title: workshop gossip
events.premise: {b} drops by {place}. {self} puts the tools down: the shop next door is closing, and the owner hasn't told the staff yet.

events.title: the money
events.premise: {self} quietly tells {b} they've undercharged for years because they're scared clients will leave. They've never admitted it.

events.title: a call from home
events.premise: {self} tells {b} their dad called: he's finally retiring, and he wants to talk about the family business.

events.title: the new apprentice
events.premise: {b} visits {place}. {self} shares what everyone is whispering: the new apprentice turned out to be the boss's nephew, and nobody was told.

events.title: a family secret
events.premise: {self} tells {b} something they never mention: they left the family business after a big fight, and still haven't made up with their dad.

events.title: maybe a promotion
events.premise: {self} tells {b} they might be up for a promotion. Their manager mentioned it in the hallway, almost like a joke.

events.title: office gossip
events.premise: {b} meets {self} at {place}. {self} has gossip: two managers are up for the same job and have stopped speaking to each other.

events.title: a secret plan
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} they've been interviewing at other companies, promotion or not. Nobody at work knows.

events.title: news from work
events.premise: {self} tells {b} the company was just bought, and nobody knows yet what it means for their team.

events.title: who's leaving
events.premise: {b} visits {place}. {self} whispers the rumor: half of marketing got called into a meeting this morning and never came back to their desks.

events.title: an offer elsewhere
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} they already have an offer from another company, and haven't told their team or the house.

events.title: exam news
events.premise: {self} tells {b} they passed the exam they were sure they'd failed, and wants to celebrate.

events.title: campus gossip
events.premise: {b} meets {self} at {place}. {self} has gossip: a professor got caught reusing old exams, and half the class had the answers.

events.title: skipping class
events.premise: {self} confesses to {b} they've skipped most of their classes for weeks, and their family thinks everything is fine.

events.title: an acceptance email
events.premise: {self} shows {b} an email: they've been accepted to a semester abroad.

events.title: classmate drama
events.premise: {b} drops by {place}. {self} fills them in: two classmates broke up in the middle of a group presentation, in front of everyone.

events.title: the real reason
events.premise: {self} admits to {b} they chose their degree to make their parents happy, and they're not sure they want it anymore.

events.title: a funny regular
events.premise: {self} tells {b} about a regular who orders the same thing every day and today, finally, asked for {self}'s name.

events.title: who's flirting
events.premise: {b} visits {place} during {self}'s shift. {self} whispers: the manager has been flirting with a regular all week, and the staff have a bet going.

events.title: why they moved
events.premise: {self} tells {b} why they really moved to Tel Aviv. It's not the story they told the house on day one.

events.title: news from the shop
events.premise: {self} tells {b} the owner is renovating, so {self} might get a few weeks off, maybe unpaid.

events.title: tip jar drama
events.premise: {b} stops by {place}. {self} leans over the counter: someone has been taking money from the tip jar, and everyone is whispering about who.

events.title: tight money
events.premise: {self} quietly tells {b} they send part of every paycheck to family back home. Nobody in the house knows how tight money really is.
